answer.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ, and two independent inherited memories (memory_86, memory_31) show shortening/simplifying onboarding reliably lifts completion and activation for self-serve/SMB accounts without any flagged retention or revenue harm. This directly addresses one of the two internal metric declines using a proven lever. Promotional pricing is superficially tempting given competitor pressure on price-sensitive SMB accounts, but memory_73 explicitly flags it as damaging 30-day retention despite short-term acquisition gains — verifying its archived record confirms this is a durable, generalized risk rather than a context-specific caveat, so it's excluded from this week's single experiment slot given the objective is sustainable long-term qualified revenue, not short-term share defense. Activation messaging (memory_91) is a reasonable alternative but onboarding completion decline is more directly and specifically addressed by the onboarding-focused memories, and stacking multiple funnel fixes isn't possible with only one experiment slot. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives don't map to the acute problems observed this quarter (SMB-facing declines), so they're deprioritized. I verified memory_73 to confirm the retention-harm rationale before ruling out the competitively tempting pricing response, and memory_86 to confirm onboarding shortening's evidence quality before committing scarce experiment capacity to it.
